headline: Official Forest Alerts and Gorge Parking Reservations
reservation: Red River Gorge requires an official Forest Service permit for overnight parking between 10 PM and 6 AM. While day-use entry is generally open, individual developed campgrounds and popular cabin rentals require separate reservations through official platforms. Seasonal demand is high; check the Daniel Boone National Forest website for the latest access changes and facility closures.

days.title: Sandstone Arches and Deep Ravines

stops.name: Sky Bridge
stops.detail: Walk the high sandstone ridge for panoramic views of the Clifty Wilderness before descending the stairs to see the arch from below.

stops.name: Gray’s Arch
stops.detail: Hike through dense rhododendron to reach one of the forest's most iconic and massive natural spans.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local navigation; roads are winding and narrow.
days.note: Nada Tunnel has strict height and width limits; verify vehicle dimensions before approaching.

days.title: State Park Peaks and Creekside Trails
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Natural Bridge State Resort Park

stops.name: Natural Bridge
stops.detail: Visit this separate state-managed landmark via trail or skylift to see the 78-foot span.

stops.name: Rock Bridge Trail
stops.detail: Follow the loop to see a rare water-spanning arch and the cascades of Creation Falls.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; conditions vary by rainfall.
days.note: Natural Bridge is state-run; check Kentucky State Parks for specific seasonal facility hours.

days.title: Lake Vistas and Northern Forest Quiet

stops.name: Cave Run Lake
stops.detail: Explore the Twin Knobs area for lakeside walking or managed swimming access.

stops.name: Zilpo Scenic Byway
stops.detail: Drive the wooded peninsula for views of the 8,000-acre reservoir and diverse birdwatching.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours between the Gorge and Morehead area.
days.note: Developed beach access and boat ramps at Cave Run have specific seasonal operating dates.

intel.title: Nada Tunnel Clearance
intel.text: The historic Nada Tunnel is a single-lane passage with a 12-foot height limit. Large RVs or trailers should use KY-715 to avoid this bottleneck.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Popular Gorge trailheads like Auxier Ridge fill early on weekends. Have a secondary destination planned as roadside parking is strictly prohibited in many zones.

intel.title: Gateway Supply Points
intel.text: Stanton and Slade serve as the primary fuel and grocery hubs for the northern forest districts. Services are sparse once you enter the Clifty Wilderness area.

intel.title: Seasonal Waterfall Flow
intel.text: Waterfalls like Van Hook Falls are highly dependent on recent precipitation. Aim for spring months for active flows; summer heat may reduce falls to a trickle.

intel.title: Offline Map Necessity
intel.text: Cellular reception is unreliable in deep sandstone ravines. Download maps for the Slade and London districts before leaving gateway towns.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at Blue Grass Airport (LEX) and stop in Lexington or Stanton for full groceries before checking into a Slade-area cabin.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger car suits most paved roads, but high-clearance vehicles are recommended for gravel forest service roads; check rental terms for unpaved surfaces.
plan.goldenHour: Chimney Top Rock provides an unobstructed westward view of the gorge, though cliff-edge safety is critical as light fades.
